advisor_description: A stately canopy oak (50–70 ft) featuring two-toned lustrous emerald foliage with downy silver undersides and golden-bronze fall color, exceptionally adaptable to heavy clay and periodic standing water ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280712)). Functions as an indispensable keystone anchor in rain gardens, bioswales, and open woodland matrices ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/swwh_oak.html)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune branches only during dormant season (before April 1) to prevent fungal Oak Wilt transmission ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280712)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide deep watering every 2–3 weeks during the first two summers until established ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280712)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave fallen oak leaves in mulch rings under the canopy to shelter overwintering pupae and insulate tree root zone ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.winter: Protect young sapling trunks with wire tree guards or wraps to prevent winter deer buck rub and rodent gnawing ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280712)).
maintenance_guide.division: Deep taproot; do not divide or transplant once established ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280712)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Keystone host supporting 450+ caterpillar species including Imperial Moth (*Eacles imperialis*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Eacles-imperialis)), Polyphemus Moth (*Antheraea polyphemus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Antheraea-polyphemus)), Banded Hairstreak (*Satyrium calanus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Satyrium-calanus)), and Juvenal's Duskywing (*Erynnis juvenalis*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Erynnis-juvenalis)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Celastrina-neglectamajor), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/black_cohosh.htm)

advisor_description: An extraordinary deciduous native holly (6–10 ft) producing breathtaking masses of brilliant scarlet berries that cling tightly to bare winter branches, creating an unmatched winter spectacle ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276156)). Indispensable for rain gardens, bioswales, pond margins, and shrub borders (requires a male pollinator nearby) ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/winterberry.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Provide consistent moisture during dry periods ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276156)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Protect berry clusters from premature netting if holiday harvest is desired ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Do not divide. Plant containerized male and female plants within 50 feet ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276156)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Henry's Elfin butterfly (*Callophrys henrici*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Callophrys-henrici)); small flowers attract native sweat bees and honeybees.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Berries soften after winter freezes to feed Eastern Bluebirds, American Robins, Hermit Thrushes, and Cedar Waxwings ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/winterberry.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Rake off heavy smothering leaves in early spring to expose emerging flower buds ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide partial shade and well-drained, organic-rich soil; drought tolerant once established ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281151)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Early spring blooms provide essential nectar for queen bumblebees and native long-tongued bees. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Hummingbirds frequently visit the early spring blooms; rhizomes are resistant to deer browsing ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281151)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Gently clear fallen leaves from around basal rosettes in spring to prevent crown smothering ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278870)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Requires consistently moist to wet soils; do not allow root zone to dry out completely in summer ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278870)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave seed stalks standing so fine seeds can scatter onto moist surrounding soil to replenish colony ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.winter: Ensure basal winter rosettes receive light; do not bury under heavy layers of woodchips ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278870)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide basal rosette offshoots in early spring every 2–3 years to maintain long-term vigor ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278870)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Primary nectar source for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds (*Archilochus colubris*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Archilochus-colubris)); flowers visited by large swallowtail butterflies.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Specially co-evolved floral structure transfers pollen onto the heads of foraging hummingbirds ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/cardinal.htm)).

wildlife_ecological_value:

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Specially co-evolved floral structure transfers pollen onto the heads of foraging hummingbirds ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/cardinal.htm)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Archilochus-colubris), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/cardinal.htm)

advisor_description: A majestic architectural native perennial (3–5 ft) forming a huge shrub-like mound of enormous compound leaves, bearing frothy greenish-white flower panicles in July followed by heavy drooping clusters of dark purple berries ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276593)). maintenance_guide.summer: Water during hot summer droughts to reduce early foliage dormancy or leaf drop ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281049)).

Indispensable for rain gardens, bioswales, sunny borders, and monarch waystations ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/sw_milkweed.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Provide consistent moisture during severe summer droughts ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276790)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Vanilla-fragrant nectar feeds dozens of butterfly species; silk from seed pods is used by goldfinches to line nests ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/sw_milkweed.htm)).

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Blooms require strong bumblebees (*Bombus*) to pry open the petals, providing exclusive nectar rewards ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287080)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Euphydryas-phaeton), [Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287080)

advisor_description: A rugged native ninebark (5–8 ft) featuring peeling, exfoliating bark, dense white to pink flower umbels in late spring, and copper-red seed capsules against rich green foliage ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286432)). Superb for erosion control, bioswales, sunny screening hedges, and tough clay banks ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/ninebark.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back woody dead stalks to 3 inches in late spring at 50°F+ ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Chelsea chop: cut stems back by half in early June to promote sturdy, compact branching and prevent flopping ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277437)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave golden seedheads intact through winter for goldfinches and winter songbirds ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide expanding rhizomatous clumps every 3 years in early spring to contain spread ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277437)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Keystone host for Silvery Checkerspot (*Chlosyne nycteis*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Chlosyne-nycteis)), Painted Lady (*Vanessa cardui*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Vanessa-cardui)), and specialist bees (*Melissodes agilis*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Melissodes-agilis)). Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Heavy seed yields provide crucial high-fat winter nutrition for goldfinches, nuthatches, and chickadees ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277437)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut down towering dead stalks in spring after 50°F+ temperatures ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave tall seed scapes standing for goldfinches and chickadees to perch and feed ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Massive woody taproot; do not divide or transplant mature specimens ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277363)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Silphium Borer Moth (*Papaipema silphii*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papaipema-silphii)) and specialist long-horned bees (*Melissodes*).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Goldfinches balance on tall scapes to extract nutrient-rich sunflower seeds all winter ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/pr_dockx.htm)).

wildlife_ecological_value:
**Host Plant Value:** Larval host for Silphium Borer Moth (*Papaipema silphii*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papaipema-silphii)) and specialist long-horned bees (*Melissodes*).

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Goldfinches balance on tall scapes to extract nutrient-rich sunflower seeds all winter ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/pr_dockx.htm)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papaipema-silphii), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/pr_dockx.htm)

advisor_description: A handsome clump-forming forest sedge (6–10 in) with fine grassy foliage producing distinctive early spring flowering spikes with prominent pale green bracts ([Grow Native!](https://grownative.org/native_plants/james-sedge/)). Ideal for rich shaded woodland understories, calcareous slopes, and naturalized matrices ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/grasses/plants/james_sedge.htm)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Trim back ragged winter foliage in spring (at 50°F+) as early bloom spikes emerge ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for sedge skippers and leaf-mining moths.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Seeds feature fleshy appendages (elaiosomes) collected and dispersed by native ants (myrmecochory) ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/grasses/plants/james_sedge.htm)).

advisor_description: A fast-blooming native plains coreopsis (1.5–3 ft) bearing profuse daisy blossoms with bright golden-yellow petals surrounding deep mahogany-red centers on airy, branching stems from June through September ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277179)). Perfect for rapid color in meadows, borders, and pollinator patches ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277179)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Allow self-sown seeds to germinate in spring; thin seedlings if crowded ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Deadhead spent blooms in midsummer if a tidy appearance and prolonged bloom is desired ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277179)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave final seedheads to self-sow and replenish the annual/biennial colony naturally ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Annual/biennial; propagate via seed ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277179)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Tiny seeds feed native grassland sparrows, goldfinches, and mourning doves ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277179)).

advisor_description: A regal native blue vervain (3–5 ft) producing candelabra-like spires of tiny, intense violet-blue flowers from July through September above handsome lanceolate leaves ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287444)). Indispensable for rain gardens, bioswales, retention margins, and moist meadow plantings ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/bl_vervain.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back dead stalks to 8–18 inches in late spring at 50°F+ ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave upright candelabra seed spikes intact to provide winter food for songbirds ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide fibrous crowns every 3–4 years in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287444)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for the Common Buckeye butterfly (*Junonia coenia*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Junonia-coenia)) and specialist bee *Verbenae andrena*. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Nutritious seeds are eaten by Cardinals, Field Sparrows, Juncos, and Bobwhite Quail ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/bl_vervain.htm)).
wildlife_detail.sources: [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Junonia-coenia), [Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/bl_vervain.htm)

wildlife_ecological_value:
**Host Plant Value:** Larval host for the Common Buckeye butterfly (*Junonia coenia*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Junonia-coenia)) and specialist bee *Verbenae andrena*. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Junonia-coenia), [Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/wetland/plants/bl_vervain.htm)

advisor_description: A stately, shrub-like native Maryland senna (3–6 ft) featuring tropical-looking pinnate foliage that folds at night and magnificent terminal clusters of bright golden-yellow pea flowers with dark brown anthers in late summer, followed by hanging black seed pods ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280479)). Ideal for bioswales, sunny borders, and hedgerows ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/savanna/plants/md_senna.html)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut dead woody stems to the ground in spring after sustained 50°F+ temperatures ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave hanging black legume pods for winter structural interest and gamebird forage ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Primary larval host for Cloudless Sulphur (*Phoebis sennae*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Phoebis-sennae)), Sleepy Orange (*Abaeis nicippe*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Abaeis-nicippe)), and Little Yellow butterflies.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Extrafloral nectaries at leaf bases feed beneficial parasitoid wasps and predatory ants; seeds feed Northern Bobwhite ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/savanna/plants/md_senna.html)).

advisor_description: A cheerful native celandine poppy (12–18 in) opening in early spring with 2-inch, brilliant butter-yellow 4-petaled blossoms above deeply lobed, blue-green oak-like foliage, followed by bristly nodding seed pods ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=284856)). A superb spring ephemeral groundcover for shaded borders and woodland gardens ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/cel_poppy.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Allow self-sown seeds to establish; clear away old leaves gently at 50°F+ ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide partial to full shade and rich organic moisture; may go dormant in dry summer heat ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=284856)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide rhizomatous crowns in early spring or immediately after flowering ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=284856)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Early spring blossoms provide vital pollen for newly emerged queen bumblebees and native mining bees. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Seeds bear nutrient-rich fleshy elaiosomes gathered and planted by woodland ants ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/cel_poppy.htm)).

wildlife_ecological_value:

advisor_description: A versatile native chokecherry (20–30 ft) erupting in late spring with 3–6 inch cylindrical racemes of fragrant white flowers, yielding heavy clusters of tart purple-black cherries ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286359)). An indispensable keystone species for naturalized borders, windbreaks, and bird gardens ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/chokecherry.html)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune out dead wood and remove unmanaged root suckers in late winter while dormant ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286359)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Water moderately during first 2 years; exceptional drought tolerance once rooted ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286359)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave remaining fruit clusters for migrating thrushes and robins ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Remove suckers with roots in early spring for propagation; do not divide mature trees ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286359)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Keystone host supporting 450+ caterpillar species including Eastern Tiger Swallowtail (*Papilio glaucus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papilio-glaucus)), Coral Hairstreak (*Satyrium titus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Satyrium-titus)), and Cecropia Moth (*Hyalophora cecropia*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Hyalophora-cecropia)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Cherries feed over 70 species of birds; early blossoms sustain queen bumblebees and solitary mining bees ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/chokecherry.html)).

advisor_description: A robust native hairy alumroot (1–2 ft tall, 2 ft wide) forming large mounding rosettes of velvety lobed leaves, sending up airy cloud-like sprays of creamy white blossoms from August to October ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286873)). Outstanding groundcover for dry shaded borders, rock gardens, and north-facing foundation beds ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286873)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until daytime temps consistently exceed 50°F before trimming away tattered overwintered leaves at the crown ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Host for specialist native bees (*Colletes*) and larvae of American Alumroot Borer Moth (*Papaipema*).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Airy late-summer flower wands provide nectar for hummingbirds, bees, and hoverflies ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286873)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Water moderately during fruit swell in midsummer; highly drought tolerant thereafter ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286905)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide rooted suckers in early spring or take dormant hardwood cuttings ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286905)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Sweet berries feed Catbirds, Brown Thrashers, Robins, and small native mammals ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286905)).

Excellent for shaded woodland borders, north-facing walls, and winter interest borders ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/witch_hazel.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Perform any structural pruning in late winter (January–February) while fully dormant to prevent beetle transmission of oak wilt ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280756)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide supplemental deep watering during severe drought in first 2 years of establishment ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280756)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Allow leaf litter to decompose under canopy to nourish soil mycelium and shelter overwintering pupae ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.winter: Protect young trunk base with wire cages to prevent winter rodent and deer damage ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280756)).
maintenance_guide.division: Deep root network; do not divide or transplant once established ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280756)).

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Essential late-season nectar feast for migrating Monarch butterflies; seeds sustain American Goldfinches all winter ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=292654)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Phyciodes-tharos), [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Andrena-asteris), [Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation), [Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=292654)

advisor_description: A dependable native fox sedge (1.5–3 ft) forming fountain-like clumps crowned in early summer with bristly, coppery-brown flowering spikes resembling the bushy tail of a fox ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279746)). Exceptional for rain gardens, retention basins, bioswales, and moist sunny meadows ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279746)).

maintenance_guide.division: Divide shallow creeping rhizomes in early spring or early autumn to expand groundcover ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=276757)).

An enduring architectural matrix plant for sunny borders, meadows, and prairie restorations ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/wild_quininex.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune unwanted root suckers in early spring to maintain a single-stemmed tree form rather than a colonial thicket ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=275970)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Maintain consistent soil moisture during midsummer fruit swell ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=275970)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Harvest ripe pawpaw fruits in September as they soften and emit a tropical mango-banana scent ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Taprooted; propagate via fresh stratified seed or dormant sucker excavation; do not divide mature trees ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=275970)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Sole obligate larval host for the Zebra Swallowtail butterfly (*Eurytides marcellus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/neographium-marcellus)) and the Pawpaw Sphinx moth (*Dolba hyloeus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Dolba-hyloeus)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Fallen fruits provide rich nutritional forage for opossums, raccoons, gray foxes, and woodland mammals ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/pawpaw.htm)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Clean away collapsed foliage in early spring at 50°F+ as sky-blue flower bells appear ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide partial to full shade and moderate moisture to prevent summer dormancy ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285442)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Soft foliage provides early spring ground cover for woodland salamanders and ground beetles ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/jacob_ladder.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Emerges late in spring (May); cut dead winter vines to the ground at 50°F+ and guide vigorous new shoots onto trellis ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Pull wandering surface root runners in midsummer if containing within designated garden beds ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=284891)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Harvest ripe yellow-green maypop fruits in September–October as they soften ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide spreading root runners in early spring while dormant ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=284891)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Early-maturing seed achenes provide critical spring nutrition for ground-foraging woodland birds like Eastern Towhees and Wood Thrushes ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279721)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune out dead, crossing, or diseased twigs immediately after spring flowering completes to maintain an open vase structure ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280440)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Water moderately during extended summer droughts to prevent leaf scorch and verticillium stress ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280440)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave hanging seed pods on branches to provide late-season food for songbirds and gamebirds ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Deep taproot; do not divide or transplant mature specimens ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280440)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Henry's Elfin butterfly (*Callophrys henrici*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Callophrys-henrici)) and Redbud Leaf-folder (*Fascista cercerisella*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Fascista-cercerisella)); early spring flowers are crucial nectar for queen bumblebees (*Bombus*) and mining bees. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Seeds are consumed by Northern Bobwhite, Tufted Titmice, Chickadees, and Cardinal species ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/redbud.htm)).

advisor_description: A sturdy native prairie coreopsis (1.5–2.5 ft) bearing bright lemon-yellow daisy blossoms with golden centers in June and July above distinctive 3-lobed 'crowfoot' foliage ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277598)). maintenance_guide.summer: Provide afternoon shade or moist soil to minimize mid-summer leaf scorch ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281045)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Shear back stems to 2–3 inches in early spring at 50°F+; edge bed boundaries to contain spreading rhizomes ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Shear back by half after main spring bloom wave to stimulate fresh compact foliage ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=283036)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide shallow spreading runners in early spring or spade edge to contain boundaries ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=283036)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Day-and-night opening flowers feed both diurnal native bees and nocturnal sphinx moths ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/sh_primrosex.htm)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until sustained 50°F+ temperatures before cutting back dead winter stems to 8–18 inches ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Chelsea chop: pinch back stems by 1/3 in early June to promote dense branching and compact form ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=290710)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave fluffy seed plumes intact through fall and winter to feed goldfinches and shelter beneficial insects ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide fibrous root clumps every 3–4 years in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=290710)).

advisor_description: An enchanting native wild columbine (1–2 ft) producing exquisite nodding, spurred bell blossoms of fiery scarlet and canary-yellow in April and May above delicate, fern-like blue-green foliage ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286069)). Essential for shaded borders, rocky slopes, and early-season hummingbird feeding stations ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/wild_columbine.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Cut stems back to basal foliage after flowering if columbine leaf miners tatter leaves ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286069)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Long nectar spurs are tailored specifically for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds (*Archilochus colubris*) ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/wild_columbine.htm)).

maintenance_guide.fall: Leave rigid cones standing undisturbed through winter to feed goldfinches and native birds ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Rigid cones are a primary winter seed staple for American Goldfinches, Chickadees, and Tufted Titmice ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/pur_coneflowerx.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune root suckers in early spring if a single-trunk tree shape is desired instead of a colonial thicket ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286355)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide supplemental deep watering during prolonged summer droughts to swell fruit ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286355)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Collect fallen plums or leave for ground-foraging wildlife ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Excavate rooted suckers in late winter while dormant for propagation ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286355)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Host for Tiger Swallowtail (*Papilio glaucus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papilio-glaucus)), Red-spotted Purple, Cecropia Moth, and specialist bees including *Andrena pruni*. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Plums are eagerly sought by wild turkeys, foxes, raccoons, and songbirds; dense thorny branches provide impenetrable nesting cover ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/am_plum.htm)).
wildlife_detail.sources: [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papilio-glaucus), [Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/am_plum.htm)

advisor_description: Missouri's official state grass (4–6 ft), forming an upright blue-green clump that ignites in rich burnt-orange in autumn, topped by magnificent shimmering golden-copper flower plumes with bright yellow stamens ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285219)). A cornerstone keystone for sunny prairies, meadows, and large perennial borders ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285219)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back to 3 inches in late spring at 50°F+ as warm-season soil temperatures rise ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave tall upright stems and golden seed plumes intact for winter structure and wildlife seed ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide dense clumps in spring every 4–5 years to maintain vigor ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285219)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Nutritious seeds feed over 20 species of native songbirds; thick bunchgrass bases shelter overwintering quail ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285219)).

Serves as an elegant groundcover matrix for shaded borders, rock gardens, and woodland path margins ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286871)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until daytime temperatures consistently exceed 50°F before trimming away tattered overwintered leaves at the crown ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.winter: Apply 1–2 inches of light mulch around root crowns in late November to prevent frost heaving in exposed beds ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286871)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide mature woody rootstocks every 3–4 years in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286871)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Host for specialist native bees (*Colletes* and *Lasioglossum*) and larvae of the American Alumroot Borer Moth (*Papaipema* species).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Airy spring flowers provide essential early nectar for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds, hoverflies, and solitary bees ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=286871)).

advisor_description: An early-blooming native Ozark witch hazel (6–10 ft) producing highly fragrant spicy-scented, ribbon-like copper-red to yellow blossoms in mid to late winter (January–March), defying ice and snow ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281022)). Thrives in stream banks, rain gardens, and foundation borders ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281022)).

maintenance_guide.spring: Prune out suckers or shape branches immediately after late-winter flowering finishes ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281022)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Maintains excellent health in both gravelly creek beds and heavy landscape clay with periodic moisture ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281022)).

Ideal for stream bank stabilization, rain gardens, and wet wildlife screening borders ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279336)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Excels in saturated, poorly drained, and periodically flooded soils in sun to partial shade ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=279336)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Water moderately during first season; remarkably heat and drought tolerant once rooted ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=242332)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Deadhead spent flowers in July to promote continuous blooming through late summer ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277306)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Seeds provide high-energy nutrition for American Goldfinches, Field Sparrows, and Bobwhite Quail ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/sand_coreopsisx.htm)).

advisor_description: A tough native Parlin's pussytoes (6–12 in) forming a dense, weed-suppressing groundcover carpet of broad, silvery-felted basal leaves, sending up fuzzy white-and-pink flower clusters resembling kitten paws in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277134)). Ideal for dry shaded borders, rocky slopes, and poor clay soils ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277134)).

Excellent for screens, naturalized woodland edges, and wildlife borders ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/nannyberry.html)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back stems to 2–3 inches in late spring (at 50°F+) as soil warms in May before new growth shoots appear ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave stiff upright stems and fluffy plumes intact through fall and winter for seed foraging and snow cover ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide dormant clumps in early spring just as green shoots begin if center dies out after 5–7 years ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285323)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for 9+ native skipper butterflies including Swarthy Skipper (*Nastra lherminier*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Nastra-lherminier)), Cobweb Skipper, and Dusted Skipper.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Fluffy seedheads provide vital winter calories for American Goldfinches, Juncos, and native mice ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285323)).
wildlife_detail.sources: [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Nastra-lherminier), [Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285323)

advisor_description: An indispensable keystone native wild bergamot (2–4 ft) bearing fragrant minty foliage topped from July to September by dense mop-head clusters of lavender-pink tubular blossoms ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281404)). Essential pollinator anchor for sunny meadows, rain gardens, borders, and monarch waystations ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/wld_bergamotx.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until daytime temperatures exceed 50°F before cutting dead stalks to 8–18 inches ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Chelsea chop: pinch stems back by 1/3 in early June to promote dense bushy growth and prevent lodging ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281404)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave aromatic button seedheads intact through winter to feed native songbirds ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide fibrous rhizomatous clumps every 3 years in early spring to maintain center vigor ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=281404)).

wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: High-sugar tubular flowers are heavily favored by Ruby-throated Hummingbirds and long-tongued bumblebees (*Bombus pensylvanicus*) ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/wld_bergamotx.htm)).

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Lipid-rich red autumn drupes provide vital high-energy fuel for migrating Wood Thrushes, Hermit Thrushes, Catbirds, and Vireos ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/spicebush.htm)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papilio-troilus), [Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Callosamia-promethea), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/spicebush.htm)

advisor_description: A showstopping native rough blazing star (2–3 ft) bearing distinctive rounded, button-like flower heads of electric magenta-purple spaced along stiff upright stalks in August and September ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=277341)). An unrivaled nectar magnet for sunny prairie borders, rock gardens, and monarch waystations ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/rgh_blazingstarx.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Harvest tight curled fiddleheads as a spring delicacy or allow them to unfurl; clear away dead previous-year fronds at 50°F+ ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Requires consistent moisture in shade; may enter early dormancy if allowed to dry out ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285874)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide creeping rhizome runners in early spring while dormant ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285874)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Ostrich Fern Borer Moth (*Papaipema speciosissima*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papaipema-speciosissima)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Stately frond colonies provide sheltered foraging grounds for Wood Thrushes and American Toads ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/grasses/plants/ostrich_fern.htm)).

advisor_description: A striking native American beautyberry (4–6 ft) famous for its tight, dazzling clusters of iridescent magenta-purple berries encircling gracefully arching stems in autumn, persisting after leaf drop ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287477)). maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut stems back to 12–18 inches in late winter (50°F+) to encourage dense new fruiting wood ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287477)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide moderate moisture in full sun to part shade; highly drought-resilient once rooted ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287477)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Protect berry clusters from early pruning so songbirds can feed into winter ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Do not divide. Propagate via softwood cuttings in summer or seeds in autumn ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287477)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Rustic Sphinx (*Manduca rustica*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Manduca-rustica)); summer blossoms buzz with long-tongued native bees.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Over 40 species of songbirds devour the purple berries, including Northern Mockingbirds, Cardinals, and Brown Thrashers ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287477)).

advisor_description: A premier native shade tree (30–50 ft) featuring smooth beech-like gray bark, bright green pinnate foliage turning golden-amber in autumn, and cascading 12-inch wisteria-like panicles of intensely fragrant white flowers in late spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280286)). Outstanding lawn and shade tree specimen ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/yl_wood.html)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Prune branches only in summer after full leaf emergence to prevent excessive sap bleeding ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280286)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Deep soak every 2–3 weeks during the first two summers of establishment ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280286)).
maintenance_guide.division: Deep taprooted legume; do not divide. Plant containerized saplings into well-drained loams ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=280286)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Flowers provide profuse nectar for queen bumblebees (*Bombus*) and long-tongued native bees. Specialist bees and native pollinators are supported ([Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Hanging legume pods feed Northern Bobwhite and small woodland rodents in late winter ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/yl_wood.html)).

wildlife_ecological_value:

**Wildlife & Ecological Interactions:** Hanging legume pods feed Northern Bobwhite and small woodland rodents in late winter ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/yl_wood.html)).

**Conservation & Scientific Sources:** [Xerces Society: Pollinator Conservation](https://xerces.org/pollinator-conservation), [Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/trees/plants/yl_wood.html)

advisor_description: An extraordinary native Indian pink (1–2 ft) producing upright one-sided floral cymes of brilliant scarlet tubular flowers that flare open at the tips into 5-pointed, canary-yellow starry stars in June ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282481)). The ultimate showstopping focal accent for shaded borders and woodland gardens ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/woodland/plants/indian_pink.html)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Provide consistent moisture during fruit development ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278942)).

advisor_description: The stately native garden phlox (3–5 ft) producing massive pyramidal flower panicles of fragrant rose-pink to magenta blossoms from July through September above upright stems with lanceolate leaves ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285435)). An indispensable high-summer focal anchor for borders, rain gardens, and cottage matrices ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/savanna/plants/sm_phlox.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Medium Maintenance. Benefits from targeted mid-season care (such as Chelsea chopping or sucker pruning) and spring cutback timing to sustain peak vigor and compact garden form.

maintenance_guide.summer: Water at soil level during severe drought to prevent powdery mildew stress; provide good air circulation ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285435)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave seed capsules for winter bird foraging ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide fibrous root crowns every 3–4 years in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285435)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for the Phlox Moth (*Schinia indiana*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Schinia-indiana)) and visited by tiger swallowtails and clearwing moths.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Deep tubular flowers provide abundant nectar for Ruby-throated Hummingbirds and large butterfly species ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/savanna/plants/sm_phlox.htm)).

advisor_description: An exceptional native roundleaf ragwort (1–2 ft) forming an evergreen emerald rosette carpet that erupts in April and May with cheerful clusters of bright golden-yellow daisy blossoms on upright stems ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=292089)). The ultimate living green mulch for shaded borders, woodland edges, and under trees ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/savanna/plants/rl_ragwort.html)).

maintenance_guide.summer: Highly drought-tolerant once established in shade; suppresses weeds throughout summer ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=292089)).

advisor_description: The undisputed king of the tallgrass prairie (5–8 ft) with silvery blue-green summer foliage that blazes in shades of bronze, copper, and ruby in autumn, topped by distinctive 3-parted 'turkey foot' flower spikes ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285262)). Best suited for meadow restorations, bioswales, and expansive sunny boundaries ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285262)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut back to 3–4 inches in late spring (at 50°F+) before vigorous warm-season growth begins ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave towering stems standing through winter to catch drifting snow and feed birds ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide large crowns in early spring every 5–7 years ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285262)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Delaware Skipper, Byssus Skipper (*Problema byssus*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Problema-byssus)), and Arogos Skipper.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: High-carbohydrate seeds sustain winter sparrows, finches, and wild turkeys; dense stalks create crucial winter shelter ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=285262)).

advisor_description: A magnificent native woolly rose mallow (4–6 ft) bearing massive 6–8 inch white or pale pink crepe-paper blossoms with deep crimson-red throats from July through September above velvety heart-shaped leaves ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282628)). A showstopping keystone anchor for rain gardens, bioswales, pond margins, and moist borders ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282628)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Cut dead woody stalks back to 4–6 inches in late spring at 50°F+ (emerges late in May) ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.summer: Provide consistent moisture; excels in standing water and saturated soils in full sun ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282628)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave velvety seed capsules for winter bird foraging ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Massive woody root crown; divide in early spring or propagate via seed ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282628)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for specialist Hibiscus Bee (*Ptilothrix bombiformis*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Ptilothrix-bombiformis)) and Io Moth (*Automeris io*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Automeris-io)).
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Massive blossoms are visited by hummingbirds, bumblebees, and specialist native bees ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=282628)).

advisor_description: A commanding architectural native Culver's root (3–6 ft) featuring upright stems encircled by handsome whorls of lance-shaped leaves, topped in midsummer by elegant candelabras of dense, branching white-to-pale-blue floral wands ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287000)). An indispensable vertical accent for rain gardens, bioswales, and sunny borders ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/culverx.htm)).

maintenance_guide.summary: Low Maintenance. Requires minimal care once established. Adhere to conservation cutback practices (sustained 50°F+ spring timing) to protect cavity-nesting bees and songbirds.
maintenance_guide.spring: Wait until daytime temperatures exceed 50°F before cutting dead stalks to 8–18 inches ([Xerces Society: Nesting Resources](https://xerces.org/publications/guidelines/nesting-overwintering-habitat)).
maintenance_guide.fall: Leave slender candelabra seed spikes intact for winter architectural structure and songbird foraging ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Divide woody crowns every 4–5 years in early spring ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=287000)).

wildlife_detail.host_insects: Larval host for Culver's Root Borer Moth (*Papaipema sciata*) ([Butterflies and Moths of North America](https://www.butterfliesandmoths.org/species/Papaipema-sciata)) and visited by hundreds of native bee species.
wildlife_detail.wildlife_users: Tall floral candelabras are a high-value landing pad for swallowtails, monarchs, and hummingbirds ([Illinois Wildflowers](https://www.illinoiswildflowers.info/prairie/plantx/culverx.htm)).

advisor_description: An exceptional small tree (12–20 ft) featuring extraordinarily glossy, leathery dark green leaves that ignite in deep crimson-purple fall color, with rusty-downy flower buds and sweet blue-black fruit ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278962)). Highly adaptable to hot, dry, rocky limestone glades and sunny borders ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278962)).

maintenance_guide.fall: Leave drupes on branches for fall and winter songbird feeding ([Xerces Society: Leave the Leaves](https://xerces.org/leave-the-leaves)).
maintenance_guide.division: Do not divide. Plant containerized specimens into full sun to part shade ([Missouri Botanical Garden PlantFinder](https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278962)).
